newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambia rail strike threatens ZCCM shipments.
newsitem.headline: Zambia rail strike threatens ZCCM shipments.

text.p: Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) said on Wednesday sporadic strikes by Zambia Railway workers could hamper its operations.

"So far, the strike has not affected us seriously, as we keep reasonable stocks. However, it could pose serious problems for us if it persisted for two or three weeks," ZCCM's corporate affairs manager Pius Mambo told Reuters.
Mambo said all of ZCCM's exports and imports, including copper concentrate, coal and acid were transported by Zambia Railway.
"We had some acid tied up in Zimbabwe for a day, but we have moved it now. We are not facing any serious problems at present," he said.
About 1,000 Zambia Railway empoyees stopped work again on Tuesday after calling off a strike last week.
The workers are demanding improved conditions of service and the removal of managing director Clement Mambwe, whom they accuse of mismanagement.
On Wednesday the Zambia Railways board said it would penalise strikers.

"The board is dismayed and appalled by the behaviour of the top union leadership who went around urging workers to go on strike, knowing fully well that the procedure for such action had not been followed," company board chairman Patrick Chamunda said.
"The board considers the strike...as illegal and all workers who stayed away on account of this strike will be disciplined," he added.
